services.method: Per country: sold_to_rus = the country's services exports to Russia (money earned from Russia, incl. Russian tourists' spending there); bought_from_rus = its services imports from Russia (money paid to Russia). EUR bn, 2021 baseline and 2022-2026 (2026 = Jan-Aug). Central = the country's own reported figure where one exists (Eurostat bop_its6_det for EU/EFTA/candidates/TUR 2021-2025; else BaTiS reported "N" series from national sources), low = min(0.9 x reported, BaTiS balanced), high = max(1.15 x reported, min(BaTiS balanced, 2 x reported)). Where no national report exists (China, UAE, India, Kazakhstan etc.), central = OECD-WTO BaTiS balanced estimate, range 0.6-1.5x. Years without data (2025 for non-Eurostat countries) = 2024 x Bank of Russia growth by flow (Russian travel imports +27%, other services imports +7%, services exports +9%, in USD), range widened 0.8/1.25. Jan-Aug 2026 = 2025 x (H1-2026 + 2/3 of Q3-2025 scaled by H1 growth)/2025, from Bank of Russia quarterly BoP; range widened 0.8/1.25. Russia's own totals are larger than the sum over countries (BaTiS under-allocates the 2023-2025 surge in Russians' travel spending abroad); that residual (unallocated, below) is added to each country's HIGH bound by its share of BaTiS travel credits (sold) or services imports from Russia (bought), capped at its central value. USD->EUR at ECB yearly averages.

GRC.oil_shipping_note: Freight earned by Greek-owned tankers carrying Russian crude, NOT included in sold_to_rus (charterers are mostly non-Russian traders, so Greek BoP books little of it against Russia; some overlap possible). Jul 2023-Jun 2026: FT analysis (Jul 2026) >= USD 3.8bn for Greek owners (Dynacom >= 0.915bn, Olympic >= 0.404bn), spread by year with Greek-share trend (low 2024, rising 2025-26; S&P: G7-linked tankers lifted 36.2% of Russian crude in Jul 2026). 2022 and Jan-Jun 2023 modelled (D): ~1.0bn bbl (Mar-Dec 2022) / 0.6bn bbl (H1 2023) seaborne crude x Greek share 30-50% / 25-40% x freight USD 4-10 / 8-15 per bbl; products excluded (high bound raised for them). Overlap: if CREA values Russian oil at delivered prices, this freight sits inside fossil-fuel payments to Russia on the map; it is money paid to Greek owners, not to Russia. Other G7 owners/insurers (CYP/MLT flags are mostly Greek-owned; UK/Norwegian P&I insurance premiums ~<EUR 0.1bn/yr) are not quantified.

upper_bound.errors_and_omissions_sign: negative in every year 2021-2026 (net unrecorded OUTFLOW from Russia: USD -1.0bn 2021, -6.1bn 2022, -9.3bn 2023, -9.7bn 2024, -13.3bn 2025, -9.4bn H1 2026)
upper_bound.note: Bank of Russia net errors and omissions are negative throughout, i.e. Russia's books show more money leaving than recorded; hidden net payments TO Russia larger than |E&O| would need equally large hidden outflows, so |E&O| is a soft upper bound on net hidden flows, not on gross ones. Gold upper bound: exportable Russian gold <= ~250 t/yr (mine output 330-345 t per WGC/Metals Focus minus domestic bar, jewellery and state purchases) minus non-Western partner-recorded imports (UN Comtrade + Swissaid UAE 2024: ~137 t 2022, ~162 t 2023, ~216 t 2024, ~160 t 2025, Hong Kong ~114 t + China ~25 t for Jan-Aug 2026), valued at average gold prices (USD/kg 58.1k, 62.5k, 76.6k, 109k, 120k). Country high bounds above are not additive: their sum exceeds these joint bounds.

crypto_and_payment_agents.note: Crypto and payment agents are mostly a way to pay for trade that customs already records (Russian imports from China, Turkey, UAE, Central Asia), so they are not added to the map. No source gives volumes by counterpart country. Gross figures for scale: Garantex >USD 100bn transfers Apr 2022-Mar 2025 (TRM Labs), ~USD 96bn 2019-2025 (other estimates); sanctioned-entity crypto volumes USD 21.9bn 2023 and 14.8bn 2024 (TRM; Chainalysis 14.9bn/15.8bn incl. Iran); A7A5 rouble stablecoin (PSB-backed, issuer Old Vector, Kyrgyzstan): USD 51bn transfers to Jul 2025 (Chainalysis), USD 72bn incoming (TRM), >USD 100bn by Jan 2026 (Elliptic), but only USD 17.3bn traded on exchanges (A7A5/USDT 6.1bn = the cross-border on/off ramp). Bank of Russia (Oct 2025): crypto settlements under the experimental legal regime "have not gained wide application". Payment agents: Russia->Kyrgyzstan bank payments USD 2.8bn in 2023 (USD 0.37bn back), fees up to 3%; agent margins of 1-3% on tens of billions of trade would be USD 0.3-2bn/yr paid by Russian importers to intermediaries in KGZ/KAZ/ARM/ARE/CHN/HKG (money from Russia, not quantified per country).

private_donations.method: Private money and in-kind donations from people, companies and foundations in each country to Ukraine and Ukrainians (charity appeals, UN agencies' private income, direct gifts to Ukrainian funds such as United24, Come Back Alive and the Prytula Foundation), EUR bn per year (2026 = Jan-Aug). notes: Ranges are ~90% intervals. A = official data, B = official data with estimated parts, C = estimate from partial data, D = model or allocation with weak evidence.
Services: sold_to_rus is money earned from Russia; bought_from_rus is money paid to Russia. Do not add GRC oil_shipping_earned to sold_to_rus without checking the overlap note.

Services already include Russian tourists' spending abroad (travel credits of the destination). Russia's own travel imports rose from USD 11.4bn (2021) to 49.2bn (2025); BaTiS allocates only part of it, so the residual widens high bounds instead of being assigned to countries.

Hidden channels: the only additive items are gold flows not in the map's goods trade (UAE 2024-26, Kyrgyzstan, Hong Kong 2026 surge). Crypto, payment agents and netting settle trade that is already recorded and are not added.
Bank of Russia net errors and omissions are negative throughout (unrecorded outflows), so hidden net inflows to Russia are bounded by about |E&O| in total.
Undisclosed aid excludes what Kiel already counts and commercial sales; Germany's and Italy's published totals are largely in Kiel.

Private donations exclude government money routed through charities and Ukrainian funds, and Ukrainians' domestic giving. Poland's private help to refugees at home is reported separately (refugee_help_at_home).
